units.rightText: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice. He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.

units.leftText: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head. He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. He has plucked my hope up like a tree.
units.rightText: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head. He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.

units.leftText: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries. His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.
units.rightText: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies. His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

units.leftText: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me. My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.
units.rightText: He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me. My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.

units.leftText: Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight. I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.
units.rightText: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight. I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.

units.leftText: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother. Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.
units.rightText: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family. Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.

units.leftText: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me. My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
units.rightText: All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me. My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

units.leftText: “Have pity on me. Have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me. Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
units.rightText: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me. Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?

units.leftText: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book! That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!
units.rightText: I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book, by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.

units.leftText: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth. After my skin is destroyed, then I will see God in my flesh,
units.rightText: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth. Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.

units.leftText: whom I, even I, will see on my side. My eyes will see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me. If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,
units.rightText: I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me! If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him, ’

units.leftText: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered, “Therefore my thoughts answer me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
units.rightText: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.

units.leftText: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me. Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,
units.rightText: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply. Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,

units.leftText: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment? Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,
units.rightText: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary? Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,

units.leftText: yet he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’ He will fly away as a dream, and will not be found. Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
units.rightText: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’ He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.

units.leftText: The eye which saw him will see him no more, neither will his place see him any more. His children will seek the favor of the poor. His hands will give back his wealth.
units.rightText: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him. His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.

units.leftText: His bones are full of his youth, but youth will lie down with him in the dust. “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,
units.rightText: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust. Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,

units.leftText: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth, yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.
units.rightText: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth, yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.

units.leftText: He has swallowed down riches, and he will vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly. He will suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue will kill him.
units.rightText: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach. He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.

units.leftText: He will not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter. He will restore that for which he labored, and will not swallow it down. He will not rejoice according to the substance that he has gotten.
units.rightText: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream. He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.

units.leftText: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he will not build it up. “Because he knew no quietness within him, he will not save anything of that in which he delights.
units.rightText: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build. Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.

units.leftText: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity will not endure. In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery will come on him.
units.rightText: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure. In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.

units.leftText: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating. He will flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow will strike him through.
units.rightText: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats. Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.

units.leftText: He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him. All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire will devour him. It will consume that which is left in his tent.
units.rightText: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him. Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.

units.leftText: The heavens will reveal his iniquity. The earth will rise up against him. The increase of his house will depart. They will rush away in the day of his wrath.
units.rightText: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him. The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.

units.leftText: Then Job answered, “Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.
units.rightText: Then Job answered: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.

units.leftText: Allow me, and I also will speak. After I have spoken, mock on. As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?
units.rightText: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking. Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?

units.leftText: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth. When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.
units.rightText: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth. When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.

units.leftText: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power? Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.
units.rightText: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power? Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.

units.leftText: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them. Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don’t miscarry.
units.rightText: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them. Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.

units.leftText: They send out their little ones like a flock. Their children dance. They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
units.rightText: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about, singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.

units.leftText: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol. They tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we don’t want to know about your ways.
units.rightText: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace. Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.

units.leftText: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’ Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
units.rightText: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’ Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

units.leftText: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger? How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?
units.rightText: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction? Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?

units.leftText: You say, ‘God lays up his iniquity for his children.’ Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it. Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
units.rightText: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it. Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.

units.leftText: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off? “Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?
units.rightText: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out? Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?

units.leftText: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet. His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.
units.rightText: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease. His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.

units.leftText: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good. They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.
units.rightText: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity. But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.

units.leftText: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me. For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’
units.rightText: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me. For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’

units.leftText: Haven’t you asked wayfaring men? Don’t you know their evidences, that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, that they are led out to the day of wrath?
units.rightText: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports? Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.

units.leftText: Who will declare his way to his face? Who will repay him what he has done? Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men will keep watch over the tomb.
units.rightText: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done? He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.

units.leftText: The clods of the valley will be sweet to him. All men will draw after him, as there were innumerable before him. So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”
units.rightText: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number. So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered, “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.
units.rightText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?

units.leftText: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him that you make your ways perfect? Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?
units.rightText: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless? Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?

units.leftText: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities. For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
units.rightText: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless? For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.

units.leftText: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry. But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.
units.rightText: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished, while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.

units.leftText: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken. Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,
units.rightText: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed. Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;

units.leftText: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you. “Isn’t God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!
units.rightText: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you. Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!

units.leftText: You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness? Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn’t see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’
units.rightText: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness? Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven. ’

units.leftText: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden, who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,
units.rightText: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod? They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.

units.leftText: who said to God, ‘Depart from us!’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’ Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
units.rightText: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’ But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.

units.leftText: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them, saying, ‘Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed their remnant.’
units.rightText: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’

units.leftText: “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace. By it, good will come to you. Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
units.rightText: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you. Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.

units.leftText: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents. Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.
units.rightText: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,

units.leftText: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you. For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.
units.rightText: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you. Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.

units.leftText: You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You will pay your vows. You will also decree a thing, and it will be established to you. Light will shine on your ways.
units.rightText: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows. Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.

units.leftText: When they cast down, you will say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person. He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”
units.rightText: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly. He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”

units.leftText: Then Job answered, “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
units.rightText: Then Job answered: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.

units.leftText: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
units.rightText: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat. I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.

units.leftText: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me. Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.
units.rightText: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say. Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.

units.leftText: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge. “If I go east, he is not there. If I go west, I can’t find him.
units.rightText: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge. If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.

units.leftText: He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him. But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I will come out like gold.
units.rightText: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him. Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.

units.leftText: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned away. I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
units.rightText: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside. I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.

units.leftText: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does. For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.
units.rightText: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires. For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.

units.leftText: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him. For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.
units.rightText: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him. God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.

units.leftText: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days? There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.
units.rightText: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days? Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.

units.leftText: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
units.rightText: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge. They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

units.leftText: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children. They cut their food in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.
units.rightText: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children. They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.

units.leftText: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold. They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.
units.rightText: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold. Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.

units.leftText: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor, so that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.
units.rightText: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt. Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

units.leftText: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst. From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.
units.rightText: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty. From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.

units.leftText: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths. The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.
units.rightText: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths. When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.

units.leftText: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me.’ He disguises his face. In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.
units.rightText: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face. In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.

units.leftText: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness. “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed on the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.
units.rightText: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness! They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.

units.leftText: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol those who have sinned. The womb will forget him. The worm will feed sweetly on him. He will be no more remembered. Unrighteousness will be broken as a tree.
units.rightText: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned. The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.

units.leftText: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow. Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.
units.rightText: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow. Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.

units.leftText: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways. They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
units.rightText: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways. They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered, “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.
units.rightText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.

units.leftText: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise? How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?
units.rightText: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise? How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

units.leftText: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight; How much less man, who is a worm, and the son of man, who is a worm!”
units.rightText: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight, how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”

units.leftText: Then Job answered, “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!
units.rightText: Then Job answered: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!

units.leftText: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge! To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?
units.rightText: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight! To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?

units.leftText: “The departed spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them. Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
units.rightText: The dead tremble — those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them. Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.

units.leftText: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing. He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.
units.rightText: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing. He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.

units.leftText: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it. He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.
units.rightText: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud. He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.

units.leftText: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke. He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.
units.rightText: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke. By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.

units.leftText: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent. Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
units.rightText: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent. Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”

units.leftText: Job again took up his parable, and said, “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter
units.rightText: Job continued his discourse: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice — the Almighty, who has embittered my soul —

units.leftText: (for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils); surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness, neither will my tongue utter deceit.
units.rightText: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils, my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

units.leftText: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me. I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart will not reproach me so long as I live.
units.rightText: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die. I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me. The Wicked Man’s Portion

units.leftText: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous. For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
units.rightText: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust. For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

units.leftText: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him? Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?
units.rightText: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

units.leftText: I will teach you about the hand of God. I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty. Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?
units.rightText: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty. Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?

units.leftText: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty. If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
units.rightText: This is the wicked man’s portion from God — the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty. Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.

units.leftText: Those who remain of him will be buried in death. His widows will make no lamentation. Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
units.rightText: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them. Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,

units.leftText: he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver. He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.
units.rightText: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent. The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.

units.leftText: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not. Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.
units.rightText: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone. Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.

units.leftText: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place. For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.
units.rightText: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place. It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

units.leftText: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine. Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.
units.rightText: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined. Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.

units.leftText: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness. He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
units.rightText: Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness. Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.

units.leftText: As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire. Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.
units.rightText: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire. Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.

units.leftText: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it. The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.
units.rightText: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it. Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.

units.leftText: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots. He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.
units.rightText: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base. He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.

units.leftText: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light. “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?
units.rightText: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light. But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?

units.leftText: Man doesn’t know its price, and it isn’t found in the land of the living. The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’
units.rightText: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living. The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’

units.leftText: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price. It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
units.rightText: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver. It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.

units.leftText: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither will it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold. No mention will be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.
units.rightText: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it. Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.

units.leftText: The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won’t be valued with pure gold. Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
units.rightText: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold. From where, then, does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?

units.leftText: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky. Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’
units.rightText: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air. Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’

units.leftText: “God understands its way, and he knows its place. For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.
units.rightText: But God understands its way, and He knows its place. For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.

units.leftText: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure. When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder,
units.rightText: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters, when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,

units.leftText: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out. To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”
units.rightText: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out. And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”

units.leftText: Job again took up his parable, and said, “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;
units.rightText: And Job continued his discourse: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,

units.leftText: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness, as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was in my tent,
units.rightText: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness, when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,

units.leftText: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me, when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
units.rightText: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me, when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

units.leftText: when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street. The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.
units.rightText: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square, the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.

units.leftText: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth. The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
units.rightText: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands. The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.

units.leftText: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me, and when the eye saw me, it commended me, because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had no one to help him,
units.rightText: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me, because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.

units.leftText: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy. I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
units.rightText: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy. I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.

units.leftText: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame. I was a father to the needy. I researched the cause of him whom I didn’t know.
units.rightText: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame. I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.

units.leftText: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and plucked the prey out of his teeth. Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.
units.rightText: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth. So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.

units.leftText: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch. My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’
units.rightText: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches. My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’

units.leftText: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel. After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.
units.rightText: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel. After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.

units.leftText: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain. I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.
units.rightText: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers. If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.

units.leftText: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs. Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
units.rightText: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs. What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?

units.leftText: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation. They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom tree are their food.
units.rightText: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night. They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.

units.leftText: They are driven out from among men. They cry after them as after a thief, so that they live in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.
units.rightText: They were banished from among men, shouted at like thieves, so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

units.leftText: They bray among the bushes. They are gathered together under the nettles. They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men. They were flogged out of the land.
units.rightText: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles. A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.

units.leftText: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them. They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.
units.rightText: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them. They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

units.leftText: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me. On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet. They cast their ways of destruction up against me.
units.rightText: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence. The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.

units.leftText: They mar my path. They promote my destruction without anyone’s help. As through a wide breach they come. They roll themselves in amid the ruin.
units.rightText: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them. They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in. Job’s Prosperity Becomes Calamity

units.leftText: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud. “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.
units.rightText: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud. And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.

units.leftText: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest. My garment is disfigured by great force. It binds me about as the collar of my tunic.
units.rightText: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest. With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.

units.leftText: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes. I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.
units.rightText: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes. I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.

units.leftText: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me. You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
units.rightText: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand. You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.

units.leftText: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living. “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
units.rightText: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living. Yet no one stretches out his hand against a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.

units.leftText: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy? When I looked for good, then evil came. When I waited for light, darkness came.
units.rightText: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy? But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.

units.leftText: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me. I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.
units.rightText: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me. I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

units.leftText: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches. My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.
units.rightText: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches. My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.

units.leftText: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman? For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?
units.rightText: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin? For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?

units.leftText: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity? Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?
units.rightText: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity? Does He not see my ways and count my every step?

units.leftText: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);
units.rightText: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit, let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.

units.leftText: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands, then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
units.rightText: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands, then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.

units.leftText: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door, then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.
units.rightText: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door, then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.

units.leftText: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.
units.rightText: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged. For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.

units.leftText: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me, what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?
units.rightText: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me, what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?

units.leftText: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb? “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
units.rightText: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb? If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,

units.leftText: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);
units.rightText: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless — though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow —

units.leftText: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering; if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;
units.rightText: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak, if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,

units.leftText: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate; then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.
units.rightText: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate, then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.

units.leftText: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because of his majesty, I can do nothing. “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’
units.rightText: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower. If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security,

units.leftText: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much; if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,
units.rightText: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much, if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,

units.leftText: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth; this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above.
units.rightText: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth, this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.

units.leftText: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him (I have certainly not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);
units.rightText: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him — I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse —

units.leftText: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’ (the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
units.rightText: if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’— but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler —

units.leftText: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart, because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—
units.rightText: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart, because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside —

units.leftText: oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment! Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, and I would bind it to me as a crown.
units.rightText: (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment. Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.

units.leftText: I would declare to him the number of my steps. I would go near to him like a prince. If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
units.rightText: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)— if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,

units.leftText: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life, let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.
units.rightText: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants, then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.

units.leftText: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.
units.rightText: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes. This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,

units.leftText: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job. Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he.
units.rightText: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him. Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.

units.leftText: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled. Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old. Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.
units.rightText: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled. So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.

units.leftText: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’ But there is a spirit in man, and the Spirit of the Almighty gives them understanding.
units.rightText: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom. But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.

units.leftText: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice. Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’
units.rightText: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice. Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’

units.leftText: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say. Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.
units.rightText: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words, I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.

units.leftText: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom. God may refute him, not man;’ for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.
units.rightText: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’ But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

units.leftText: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say. Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?
units.rightText: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them. Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?

units.leftText: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion. For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.
units.rightText: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know. For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.

units.leftText: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst. I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.
units.rightText: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin. I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.

units.leftText: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man. For I don’t know how to give flattering titles, or else my Maker would soon take me away.
units.rightText: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man. For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.[’’]

units.leftText: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words. See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.
units.rightText: “But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words. Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.

units.leftText: My words will utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they will speak sincerely. The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
units.rightText: My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know. The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

units.leftText: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up. Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.
units.rightText: Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me. I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.

units.leftText: Behold, my terror will not make you afraid, neither will my pressure be heavy on you. “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,
units.rightText: Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you. Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words:

units.leftText: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me. Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.
units.rightText: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me. Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.

units.leftText: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’ “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.
units.rightText: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’ Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.

units.leftText: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters? For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.
units.rightText: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks? For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.

units.leftText: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed, then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,
units.rightText: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds, He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings

units.leftText: that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man. He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
units.rightText: to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride, to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.

units.leftText: “He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones, so that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.
units.rightText: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones, so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.

units.leftText: His flesh is so consumed away that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out. Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.
units.rightText: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude. He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.

units.leftText: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him, then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’
units.rightText: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him, to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’

units.leftText: His flesh will be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth. He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.
units.rightText: then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth. He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.

units.leftText: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me. He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life will see the light.’
units.rightText: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved. He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’

units.leftText: “Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man, to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.
units.rightText: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times, to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.

units.leftText: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak. If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.
units.rightText: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak. But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.

units.leftText: Moreover Elihu answered, “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
units.rightText: Then Elihu continued: “Hear my words, O wise men; give ear to me, O men of learning.

units.leftText: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food. Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.
units.rightText: For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food. Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.

units.leftText: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right. Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’
units.rightText: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice. Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’

units.leftText: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water, who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?
units.rightText: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water? He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.

units.leftText: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’ “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.
units.rightText: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’ Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.

units.leftText: For the work of a man he will give to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways. Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
units.rightText: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences. Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.

units.leftText: Who put him in charge of the earth? Or who has appointed him over the whole world? If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,
units.rightText: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world? If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,

units.leftText: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust. “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.
units.rightText: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust. If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.

units.leftText: Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty, who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
units.rightText: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One, who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’

units.leftText: He doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respect the rich more than the poor, for they all are the work of his hands. In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
units.rightText: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands. They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.

units.leftText: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings. There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
units.rightText: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step. There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.

units.leftText: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment. He breaks mighty men in pieces in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.
units.rightText: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment. He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.

units.leftText: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed. He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
units.rightText: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed. He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,

units.leftText: because they turned away from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways, so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.
units.rightText: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways. They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.

units.leftText: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? He is over a nation or a man alike, that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.
units.rightText: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation, that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.

units.leftText: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more. Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
units.rightText: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more. Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’

units.leftText: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know. Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:
units.rightText: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed Him? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know. Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:

units.leftText: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’ I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.
units.rightText: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’ If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.

units.leftText: Moreover Elihu answered, “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’
units.rightText: And Elihu went on to say: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’

units.leftText: that you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit will I have, more than if I had sinned?’ I will answer you, and your companions with you.
units.rightText: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’ I will reply to you and to your friends as well.

units.leftText: Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you. If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?
units.rightText: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you. If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?

units.leftText: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand? Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.
units.rightText: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand? Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.

units.leftText: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty. But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
units.rightText: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty. But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,

units.leftText: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’ There they cry, but no one answers, because of the pride of evil men.
units.rightText: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’ There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.

units.leftText: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it. How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!
units.rightText: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it. How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,

units.leftText: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance, therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”
units.rightText: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly! So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”

units.leftText: Elihu also continued, and said, “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
units.rightText: And Elihu continued: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.

units.leftText: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker. For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
units.rightText: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker. For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.

units.leftText: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding. He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives justice to the afflicted.
units.rightText: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding. He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.

units.leftText: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted. If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
units.rightText: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever. And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,

units.leftText: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly. He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.
units.rightText: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed. He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.

units.leftText: If they listen and serve him, they will spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures. But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword; they will die without knowledge.
units.rightText: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness. But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.

units.leftText: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them. They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.
units.rightText: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help. They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.

units.leftText: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression. Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.
units.rightText: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression. Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.

units.leftText: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you. Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.
units.rightText: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you. Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.

units.leftText: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength? Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.
units.rightText: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress? Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.

units.leftText: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction. Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
units.rightText: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction. Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?

units.leftText: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’? “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.
units.rightText: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’? Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
